review.comment: You set up readline correctly and trim before checking for an empty name, which handles whitespace-only input. Both outputs miss the README format: the greeting prints the literal text Hello, <line> instead of the trimmed name with Hello, <name>!, and the error should be ERROR: name is required. Next: store line.trim() in a variable, use a template literal for the greeting, and match the exact error string.

You fixed the exact error string and greeting format; readline, trim-for-empty, and rl.close() fit the lesson well. Input with surrounding spaces still prints the untrimmed line in Hello, line! instead of Hello, Bob!. Next: store line.trim() in a name variable and use it for both the empty check and the greeting.

You fixed the trim bug by storing line.trim() in name and using it for both the empty check and the greeting, so spaced input greets the trimmed name. readline, trim-before-empty, and rl.close() fit the lesson. All four acceptance cases pass. Solid match to acceptance criteria.
